name: Architectural Drawing Layer Image Dataset (ADLID)
description: Accurate layer classification in architectural drawings is a crucial step toward automating Building Information Modeling (BIM). However, this task is hindered by inconsistent layer naming and a scarcity of labeled data. In this paper, we introduce the Architectural Drawing Layer Image Dataset (ADLID), a new benchmark comprising 1,459 high-quality images converted from real-world DXF files via an automated pipeline. ADLID covers 12 common layer categories and provides a diverse testbed for evaluating classification methods. To address data scarcity, we adopt CLIP-Adapter, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach that adapts the pre-trained Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) model to the drawing domain. Extensive experiments under both full-data and few-shot settings demonstrate that CLIP-Adapter achieves 95.62% accuracy when trained on all data, and 84.51% with only 16 samples per class—significantly outperforming zero-shot CLIP and other baselines. Our work provides a strong baseline for automated drawing parsing and facilitates future research in BIM automation.
